controls.name: peek-fire-partner-target-elsewhere
controls.why: the partner is stationary, its selected target is (5,0) — neither the landing (1,0) nor the mover's target (3,0) — and the mover genuinely passes through. This is the ONLY shape rev 3 admits, and it must be shown admitting.

controls.name: peek-decline-partner-target-is-the-landing
controls.why: one fact changed from the fire twin: the partner's target is the contested cell itself. This is the standing-chopper shape — 29 of the corpus's 989 encounters.

controls.name: peek-decline-partner-target-is-the-mover-target
controls.why: both units want (3,0). This is the OSC-006 dance the pass-through test alone could not tell from a real pass-through.

controls.name: peek-decline-partner-target-none
controls.why: the partner is WAIT and `Self::wait()` sets `target:Target::None`. 960 of the corpus's 989 encounters are this row, so this control is the corpus result.

controls.name: peek-decline-partner-absent-from-map
controls.why: no entry at all for the partner — the shape a stale or incomplete map produces. It must behave exactly like Target::None, not like an unconstrained fire.

controls.name: peek-decline-empty-map
controls.why: the map exists but is empty. Fail-closed must not depend on the map being absent.

controls.name: peek-decline-mover-arrives-and-stays
controls.why: same admitting partner target as the fire twin, but the mover's own target IS the landing, so it is not passing through — it is taking the cell to keep it.
